request:
[Feature] Turtle Graphics Game for Kids 5-7

### Objective

Build a small turtle graphics web app for children aged 5-7. Children move a
visible turtle around a drawing board, turn it, and lift or lower its pen to
make simple artwork. Immediate visual feedback should make direction, distance,
right-angle turns, and drawing versus movement tangible without requiring
typing, reading code, signing in, or adult setup inside the app.

The first screen is the usable playground, not a landing page. This is creative
play, not a scored game, course, or programming-language implementation.

### Scope Baseline

The requester confirmed the age group and exactly six buttons:

1. Pen Up
2. Pen Down
3. Move Forward
4. Move Backwards
5. Turn Left 90 degrees
6. Turn Right 90 degrees

All six commands are in scope. The board, turtle artwork, pen-state feedback,
responsive controls, tests, and local launch documentation complete the feature.
There is no command editor, command history, or additional application control.

### Assumptions for Review

- Movement is one fixed-size step per activation; there is no distance input.
- The pen starts down so the first forward move draws immediately.
- One fixed ink color is enough for this pilot. The turtle remains visually
  distinct from the ink.
- Refreshing the browser starts a new drawing. A dedicated reset button,
  undo, color picker, and export can be separate follow-up features.
- The application is served locally or by an existing static host. This issue
  does not provision public hosting or change GitHub settings.

### Acceptance Criteria

### User Scenarios & Testing

**P1: Draw a first shape.** Given a fresh board, when a child alternates Move
Forward and Turn Right 90 degrees four times, then a square appears, the turtle
returns to its starting position facing up, and no extra segments appear.

**P1: Move without leaving a mark.** Given a fresh board, when a child presses
Pen Up, Move Forward, Pen Down, Move Forward, then only the second movement
draws a line. The visible pen indicator follows both pen commands.

**P2: Explore and recover at an edge.** Given the turtle has reached the top
movement boundary, another forward move leaves it in place. A backward move
brings it back into the board. No dialog interrupts play, and the controls
remain usable.

### Requirements

**REQ-001: Immediate playground.** On load, show one square drawing board,
one recognizable turtle, exactly the six buttons named above, and a short
pen-state indicator. No login, modal, instruction screen, or start button is
required before drawing. No keyboard input beyond optional button activation
is required.

**REQ-002: Initial state and coordinates.** Use a 400-by-400 logical drawing
space with the origin at its top-left, positive x to the right, and positive y
downward. Start the turtle at (200, 200), facing up, with its pen down and no
drawn segments. The coordinate system is an acceptance-test reference, not
required on-screen text for children.

**REQ-003: Forward movement.** Move Forward moves exactly 20 logical units
in the direction the turtle faces, subject to the boundary rule below. It
does not change the turtle's heading or pen state.

**REQ-004: Backward movement.** Move Backwards moves exactly 20 logical units
opposite the direction the turtle faces, subject to the same boundary rule.
It does not turn the turtle around or change the pen state.

**REQ-005: Left turn.** Turn Left 90 degrees rotates the turtle one quarter
turn counterclockwise without changing its position or drawing anything.
The heading cycle is up, left, down, right, up.

**REQ-006: Right turn.** Turn Right 90 degrees rotates the turtle one quarter
turn clockwise without changing its position or drawing anything.
The heading cycle is up, right, down, left, up.

**REQ-007: Pen up.** Pen Up changes subsequent movements to travel without
drawing. It does not move the turtle, erase artwork, or draw a mark. Repeating
Pen Up has no additional effect.

**REQ-008: Pen down.** Pen Down changes subsequent successful movements to
draw. It does not move the turtle or draw a mark by itself. Repeating Pen Down
has no additional effect. Both pen buttons remain available, with the active
mode distinguished visually and programmatically, not by color alone.

**REQ-009: Artwork semantics.** A successful pen-down movement adds exactly
one straight segment between the old and new positions. Use a fixed dark ink
stroke with rounded ends, 4 logical units wide. Existing segments persist;
turns, pen changes, and pen-up movements never modify them. The turtle cursor
is separate from the artwork and does not leave cursor-shaped trails.

**REQ-010: Safe boundaries.** Turtle-center coordinates must stay between
20 and 380 inclusive on both axes. A movement that would leave this range is
a no-op: no movement, line, wraparound, automatic turn, or pen-state change.
The whole turtle remains visible at the boundary, and another valid command
can move it away. For example, 20 consecutive forward presses from the initial
state end at (200, 20) with exactly nine drawn segments.

**REQ-011: One activation, one command.** Each completed click, tap, Enter,
or Space activation of a focused button applies exactly one command. Commands
are processed in activation order. Pointer holding must not start continuous
movement, and a tap must not be processed twice through separate touch and
click handlers. There is no queued animation or automatic drawing loop.

**REQ-012: Visible cause and effect.** The turtle has a discernible head and
orientation and is always drawn above the artwork. Movement and turns update
it immediately; pen changes update the visible Pen Up or Pen Down state in
the same interaction. Use original, self-contained turtle artwork and familiar
direction/pen symbols paired with readable button labels. Do not add tutorial
paragraphs, scoring, or celebratory interruptions.

**REQ-013: Child-friendly access.** Every button has an accessible name matching
its action, a visible keyboard-focus indicator, and a touch target of at least
56 by 56 CSS pixels. Labels may wrap but must not be clipped. All six commands
work with pointer, touch, and keyboard. The drawing surface has an accessible
name, and changes of heading and pen state have a concise nonvisual equivalent.

**REQ-014: Responsive layout without data loss.** At viewport widths of 320,
390, 768, and 1280 CSS pixels, the complete square board and all controls fit
without horizontal page scrolling, overlap, or clipped labels. Vertical page
scrolling is acceptable. The board scales visually without changing the
logical step size, turtle state, or saved segments. Resizing or changing device
orientation preserves the drawing. Controls remain operable at 200% text zoom.

**REQ-015: Predictable reset and privacy.** Refreshing the page restores the
initial state and empty board. Drawings and interactions remain in page memory
only: no cookies, browser persistence, accounts, analytics, uploads, or external
requests beyond loading the application's own static assets.

**REQ-016: Deterministic, responsive behavior.** Replaying the same finite command
sequence from the same initial state produces the same heading, pen state,
position, and ordered drawing segments. A sequence of 500 alternating forward
and backward activations remains responsive and produces exactly 500 segments
when the pen stays down; no movement is lost or duplicated. No controls depend
on an inference service or a network connection after the app's assets load.

### Key Entities

- **Turtle:** logical position, one of four headings, and pen-up/pen-down state.
- **Artwork:** the ordered line segments produced by successful pen-down moves.
- **Command:** one of the six button actions, with no child-supplied code or
  arbitrary executable content.

### Success Criteria

- A child can make the first visible line with one button activation from the
  initial screen; no setup or reading of instructions is necessary.
- The square scenario produces exactly four sides and returns to (200, 200)
  facing up. Four left turns also restore the initial heading without drawing.
- The pen-up scenario ends at (200, 160) with one segment from (200, 180) to
  (200, 160), leaving the first 20-unit movement blank.
- At all four specified viewport widths, every control remains available and
  the turtle and board remain inspectable. Desktop and touch-browser checks
  show the artwork and cursor, not only an empty drawing element.
- The page loads and the scenarios complete without uncaught browser errors
  or third-party network requests. Refreshing produces an empty board.


### Constraints and Non-goals

- Fit the implementation into at most six dependency-ordered tasks and the
  repository's existing file, job, repair, and inference budgets.
- Do not change the controller, cost accounting, migration code, workflows,
  credentials, permissions, state branch, or enforcement policy for this feature.
- Do not modify dependency manifests or lockfiles, the TypeScript configuration,
  existing baseline tests, or other protected paths. Do not add, download, or
  vendor a framework, command-language parser, rendering engine, or test library
  to work around those restrictions. Native browser graphics are sufficient
  for this six-command scope.
- No backend, public deployment, external assets, third-party font requests,
  advertising, user-generated sharing, multiplayer, or collection of children's
  personal information. Keep the experience self-contained and English-only.
- No text programming, Logo compatibility, loops, variables, procedures, blocks,
  command recording, replay UI, drawing challenges, badges, or lesson system.
- No extra application buttons, menus, adjustable distances or angles, pen-width
  control, color selection, undo/redo, reset control, save/import, or export.
- No camera, microphone, location, clipboard, or other permission prompts.
- Do not weaken coverage or security gates. Both line and branch coverage must
  meet policy and must not drop from the baseline measured for this new issue.
  Do not copy an old numerical coverage baseline into the new implementation.


### Context

This is a new feature and a fresh end-to-end exercise of the agentic SDLC
pipeline, not a continuation of issue #1 or its existing PR. The template is
[the Agentic Feature form](../.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/agentic-feature.yml).
Repository constraints are defined by [the policy](../.github/sdlc/policy.json),
[the build configuration](../tsconfig.json), and
[the validation runner](../src/validate.ts).

### Implementation and Verification Boundaries

- Place new TypeScript behavior under `src/turtle-graphics/`, browser assets
  under `apps/turtle-graphics/`, and new discovered Node tests under `test/`
  with filenames matching `test/**/*.test.ts`. Update the README and relevant
  feature documentation to describe the actual local launch procedure.
- Reuse the existing `npm run build` and Node 24.8+ toolchain. The research plan
  must specify the browser entry point, build output references, and a runnable
  local static-serving command without changing protected configuration.
- Browser modules must not import controller or Node-only modules. Keep turtle
  transitions and drawing data independently testable, using the same logic in
  the application and Node tests. Do not duplicate an engine for the browser,
  omit behavioral code from coverage, or assert only that files exist.
- Run `npm ci --ignore-scripts` and `npm run verify`. Add regression tests for
  all headings, forward/backward symmetry, turns, pen idempotence, mixed command
  sequences, all four boundaries and corners, and drawing/state preservation.
- The current required pipeline validates Node tests, not browser interactions.
  Its research plan must acknowledge that limit and describe desktop and touch
  browser verification of rendering, buttons, resize behavior, accessibility,
  and console/network errors. Use browser automation if available without
  changing protected dependencies; otherwise document explicit human checks
  at PR review. Never report a browser check as passed from Node tests alone.

### Pipeline Pilot Checks

These are checks on the existing pipeline, not features of the children's app:

1. Create a new issue with this final scope. Have an authorized repository
   writer apply `agentic-SDLC` after the text is complete. The human label event
   starts intake; the research plan still requires explicit versioned approval.
2. Confirm a new lifecycle, plan, branch, job sequence, and cost ledger are used;
   do not reuse or edit the old issue's state. The new cost history is complete
   from intake, rather than carrying a legacy-history warning.
3. Let research, decomposition, implementation, scanning, security, testing,
   validation, documentation, and final review follow the normal approved flow.
   Do not force retries or extra inference just to create spending data.
4. When the final PR is ready, inspect its runner minutes, AI credits, number
   of recorded runs, and near-limit/pre-emption counts. Actual work should have
   recorded nonzero duration and inference usage. Compare these with the issue
   status; do not invent costs or present them as dollar charges.
5. A later reconciliation with no new worker run must not charge the same work
   again. The PR must still reference the approved plan and current-commit gate
   evidence. Review the browser-verification evidence or perform the documented
   browser checks before deciding whether to merge.

plan.body:
## Summary

Build a six-button turtle graphics playground for children aged 5-7, entirely
client-side, reusing the existing Node/TypeScript toolchain without adding
dependencies, frameworks, or protected-path changes. This revision keeps the
scope and design proven on the retired `agentic/epic-19-v1` branch (used here
as reference evidence only, not as a merge source) and additionally repairs
the CodeQL finding raised against that branch's `test/turtle-graphics/ui.test.ts`
same-origin asset check, without weakening what it verifies.

## Approach

**Shared engine (`src/turtle-graphics/engine.ts`, new directory under
`sourcePaths: src/**/*.ts`, so it is not a protected top-level `src/*.ts`
file):**
- Pure, framework-free TypeScript module with no DOM or Node-only imports, so
  it runs unmodified in both Node tests and the browser (loaded as an ES
  module `<script type="module">`).
- Types: `Heading = 'up' | 'left' | 'down' | 'right'`, `PenState = 'up' |
  'down'`, `Point = { x: number; y: number }`, `Segment = { from: Point; to:
  Point }`, `TurtleState = { position: Point; heading: Heading; pen: PenState;
  segments: Segment[] }`.
- `createInitialState(): TurtleState` — position (200, 200), heading `'up'`,
  pen `'down'`, empty segments (REQ-002).
- Pure reducer `applyCommand(state, command): TurtleState` for `'penUp' |
  'penDown' | 'forward' | 'backward' | 'turnLeft' | 'turnRight'`. Returns a
  new state object on any real transition, and the *same* state reference for
  no-ops (boundary-blocked moves, idempotent pen repeats), so tests can assert
  determinism with `assert.equal` reference checks as well as `deepEqual`
  value checks (REQ-016).
- Movement math: fixed step `STEP = 20`; heading vectors `up: (0,-1), down:
  (0,1), left: (-1,0), right: (1,0)`; candidate position computed, then
  clamped-range check `20 <= x <= 380` and `20 <= y <= 380` (REQ-010). Out of
  range -> no-op (same reference). In range with pen down -> append one
  segment; pen up -> move without appending.
- Turns rotate the heading via a fixed cycle array and never touch position or
  segments (REQ-005/006).
- Pen commands only change `pen`; repeating a pen command returns the same
  reference (REQ-007/008).
- No timers, no animation queue — one call, one state transition (REQ-011,
  REQ-016).
- This matches the engine already validated (with passing Node tests) on
  `origin/agentic/epic-19-v1:src/turtle-graphics/engine.ts`, used here purely
  as design evidence.

**Browser assets (`apps/turtle-graphics/`):**
- `index.html`: single static page, one square SVG board (`id="board"`, 400x400
  logical viewBox, scaled responsively via `width: 100%` / `max-width: 400px` /
  `aspect-ratio` so REQ-014's four breakpoints — 320/390/768/1280 — all fit
  without horizontal scroll), one turtle glyph (`id="turtle"`), a pen-state
  indicator (`id="pen-indicator"` with `aria-live="polite"`, not color-only per
  REQ-008/013), and exactly six `<button data-command="...">` elements labelled
  Pen Up / Pen Down / Move Forward / Move Backwards / Turn Left 90 degrees /
  Turn Right 90 degrees, each with a `button { min-width/min-height: 56px }`
  rule and a `button:focus-visible { outline: ... }` rule with a nonzero width.
  `#controls` uses `grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(...px,
  100%), 1fr))` so it reflows instead of overflowing at narrow widths or 200%
  zoom.
- `app.js` (hand-authored plain ES-module JavaScript, **not** compiled by the
  protected root `tsconfig.json`, since `apps/**/*.ts` is outside its `include`
  globs and the root config itself must not be edited): imports
  `applyCommand`/`createInitialState` from
  `../../dist/src/turtle-graphics/engine.js` — the output of the existing
  `npm run build` — so browser behavior is identical to the tested TypeScript
  module in `src/turtle-graphics/engine.ts`, with no duplicated logic. Wires
  each button to exactly one `click` event listener (keyboard Enter/Space
  activate native `<button>` semantics for free; no separate `touchstart`
  handler avoids double-firing per REQ-011). A single `render()` re-renders
  segments, turtle position, and the pen indicator from the full state on
  every command, re-appending the turtle glyph last so it stays visually above
  the artwork (REQ-012).
- No inline event handlers, no `eval`/`Function`, no dynamic `innerHTML`
  assignment, no external script/font/analytics references, no `fetch`/
  `XMLHttpRequest` (REQ-015).

**CodeQL repair — exact URL validation in
`test/turtle-graphics/ui.test.ts` (fixes the flagged finding without weakening
the check):**
- The v1 reference test asserted same-origin assets with an unanchored
  substring check: `!ref.includes('://') && !ref.startsWith('//')`. CodeQL's
  `js/incomplete-url-substring-sanitization` class of finding flags exactly
  this pattern: testing for a scheme or protocol-relative marker anywhere in
  the string (or via `includes`) is not equivalent to correctly *parsing* the
  reference, and is fragile to representations the substring check does not
  anticipate.
- The fix keeps the same security intent (reject any reference that is not a
  same-origin relative path) but validates it exactly: anchor a scheme check
  to the start of the string with `/^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9+.-]*:/` (the RFC 3986
  URI-scheme grammar) instead of searching for `'://'` anywhere in the value,
  and keep the explicit `ref.startsWith('//')` check for protocol-relative
  references. Every `src`/`href` value in `index.html` must fail the anchored
  scheme test, fail the protocol-relative test, and additionally start with
  `./` or `../` (or be a bare relative filename) — the assertion becomes
  strictly *more* precise, not weaker, because it stops relying on `includes`
  and instead parses the leading token exactly once per candidate reference.
- No other test in `ui.test.ts` needs to change: the `eval`/`Function`/
  `innerHTML`/inline-handler checks and the `fetch`/`XMLHttpRequest` checks are
  plain negative pattern assertions on trusted, repository-authored source
  text (not sanitization gates over untrusted input), so they are outside the
  finding's scope.

**Build and local launch (no protected-path or dependency changes):**
- Reuse `npm run build` (`tsc -p tsconfig.json`, unmodified) to compile
  `src/turtle-graphics/engine.ts` to `dist/src/turtle-graphics/engine.js`.
  `apps/turtle-graphics/app.js` is committed as plain JavaScript and imports
  that build output directly, so no new build step or tsconfig change is
  needed.
- Local static serving documented in the README: `npx --yes serve
  apps/turtle-graphics` or `python3 -m http.server --directory
  apps/turtle-graphics 8080` (no new dependency; `serve` runs via `npx`
  without being added to `package.json`).

## Task Breakdown (fits in 6 tasks)

1. **Engine**: `src/turtle-graphics/engine.ts` + `test/turtle-graphics/
   engine.test.ts` covering all headings, forward/backward symmetry, both turn
   directions, pen idempotence (same-reference no-ops), mixed sequences, all
   four boundary edges and corners, the 500-command replay determinism check
   (REQ-016), and the documented square and pen-up scenarios.
2. **Browser UI**: `apps/turtle-graphics/index.html` + `app.js` wiring the six
   buttons, board rendering, pen indicator, and accessibility attributes, plus
   `test/turtle-graphics/ui.test.ts` with the anchored, exact same-origin URL
   check described above (not the unanchored `includes('://')` version).
3. **Responsive styling**: CSS for the four breakpoints, focus rings, 56x56
   touch targets, 200% zoom behavior (may be folded into task 2's `index.html`
   if the diff stays within `maxFiles`/`maxChangeBytes`; kept as a separate
   task here only if the coding task finds the combined diff too large).
4. **Security review** — existing pipeline stage, not a new task; the engine
   has no I/O and the UI has no dynamic HTML injection or external requests.
5. **Testing task**: additional regression tests only, under
   `test/turtle-graphics/`, no baseline test modification.
6. **Documentation task**: update `README.md`'s local-launch section and add
   `docs/turtle-graphics.md` (or extend `docs/architecture.md`) with the
   static-serving command and the manual browser-verification checklist below.

This uses 2-3 implementation tasks (engine, UI+styling, optionally split
styling) plus the existing testing and documentation stages, within the
6-task `maxTasks` policy limit.

## Alternatives Considered

- **Canvas vs. SVG rendering**: SVG chosen for crisp scaling and simple
  DOM-based test hooks (each segment as a `<line>`); canvas redraw-from-state
  is equally valid but harder to assert against in Node-based `ui.test.ts`
  without a DOM. Left to the coding task only if SVG proves impractical.
- **CodeQL fix via a URL-parsing library**: rejected — adding a dependency to
  parse a same-origin check is disproportionate and against the "no new
  dependency" constraint; the RFC 3986 scheme grammar is a one-line anchored
  regex and needs no library.
- **CodeQL fix via broader forbidden-substring denylist**: rejected — an
  unanchored denylist is exactly the flagged pattern; anchoring the scheme
  check at the start of the string is the precise, non-weakening fix.

## Non-Goals (per issue)

No distance/angle inputs, no reset/undo/color/export controls, no backend, no
persistence, no third-party fonts or libraries, no command language or replay
UI, no scoring or celebratory interruptions.

## Security Risks

- Client-only static assets with no network calls beyond same-origin assets:
  minimal attack surface. No user-supplied text is rendered as HTML (no
  `innerHTML` with dynamic content), avoiding DOM XSS. No external script
  sources (REQ-015).
- The one identified prior finding — imprecise same-origin URL validation in
  the UI test itself — is repaired by anchoring the scheme check, as described
  above, rather than by suppressing, weakening, or removing the assertion.

## Validation Strategy

- `npm ci --ignore-scripts && npm run verify` covers the engine via Node
  tests and coverage thresholds (80% lines / 70% branches, no drop), plus
  `tsc --noEmit` across `src/**/*.ts` and `test/**/*.ts`.
- The required pipeline's `validate` stage only runs Node tests — it cannot
  exercise the browser UI. This plan does not claim browser verification
  passes from Node tests alone.
- Manual/human browser verification checklist (to be documented in
  `docs/turtle-graphics.md` and performed by the requester or a reviewer
  before merge, since no browser-automation tool is available in this
  environment): load `apps/turtle-graphics/index.html` via a local static
  server in a desktop browser and a touch-capable device or emulator; run the
  square scenario (4x forward+right) and confirm return to (200,200) facing
  up; run the pen-up scenario and confirm exactly one visible segment from
  (200,180) to (200,160); drive the turtle to each of the four boundaries and
  confirm no-op behavior with no console/network errors (DevTools Network tab
  shows zero requests beyond the page's own assets); resize/rotate at the four
  specified widths and confirm no horizontal scroll or clipped labels;
  keyboard-tab through all six buttons and confirm visible focus and correct
  activation from Enter and Space.
- The next CodeQL/security scan of the coded UI test must show the prior
  same-origin-check finding resolved, with no new findings introduced.

## Unresolved Questions

None blocking approval. The browser-entry-point mechanism (plain JS in
`apps/`, importing the root-built `dist/src/turtle-graphics/engine.js`) and
rendering technology (SVG) are settled by the v1 reference evidence and stated
above as the approach, not left open.

## Sources Consulted

- `.sdlc-context.json` (issue #19 request, policy, job, revision feedback).
- `source/README.md`, `source/docs/architecture.md`, `source/docs/
  operations.md` (pipeline lifecycle, CodeQL gate behavior, and constraints).
- `source/docs/turtle-graphics-feature.md` (the issue's full requirements
  text, captured on `main` at commit `e56d03f`).
- `source/.github/sdlc/policy.json` (protected paths, coverage thresholds,
  task limits: `maxTasks: 6`, `sourcePaths: src/**/*.ts`, protected `src/*.ts`
  and `tsconfig.json`).
- `source/tsconfig.json`, `source/package.json` (build/test/verify commands,
  Node engine requirement).
- `source/src/domain.ts`, `source/test/domain.test.ts` (existing pure-function
  and test style conventions to follow).
- `source/src/validate.ts` (confirms only Node tests under
  `test/**/*.test.ts` are executed by the required pipeline; no browser
  automation is invoked).
- `origin/agentic/epic-19-v1` (this repository's own retired branch,
  inspected read-only via `git show`, not merged or checked out as a base):
  `src/turtle-graphics/engine.ts`, `apps/turtle-graphics/index.html`,
  `apps/turtle-graphics/app.js`, `test/turtle-graphics/engine.test.ts`, and
  `test/turtle-graphics/ui.test.ts` — used per the revision feedback as design
  reference, with the same-origin URL check in `ui.test.ts` specifically
  identified as needing the anchored-scheme fix described above.

Independent security review of the turtle-graphics feature diff (baseSha e56d03fc01ef321280fd8c07b527ecb7c9cb33c8 -> headSha 6c454e1b225dc5976271ba692f2918730d714a64, branch agentic/epic-19-v2). Reviewed diff scope: src/turtle-graphics/engine.ts (new, 118 lines, pure TypeScript reducer), apps/turtle-graphics/app.js (new, 81 lines, hand-authored browser entry point), apps/turtle-graphics/index.html (new, 140 lines, static markup/CSS), README.md documentation additions, and the test-stage's added test files (test/turtle-graphics/engine-requirements.test.ts, ui-requirements.test.ts). No changes to package.json, package-lock.json, tsconfig.json, .github/**, or any other protected path -- confirmed via `git diff --stat` scoped to those paths returning empty, so no new dependencies or workflow/trust-boundary changes were introduced.

Findings:
- engine.ts is a pure, side-effect-free state reducer (createInitialState/applyCommand) with no I/O, no eval/Function construction, no external input parsing; movement is clamped to a fixed MIN_COORD(20)/MAX_COORD(380) board via inRange(), preventing unbounded/out-of-range state.
- app.js renders exclusively via createElementNS + setAttribute/textContent (no innerHTML, no document.write, no dangerouslySet-style APIs), so there is no DOM-based XSS vector; all rendered values (coordinates, heading, pen state) originate from the closed Command union, not from arbitrary user text.
- app.js/index.html make no network requests, and grep confirmed no use of document.cookie, localStorage, sessionStorage, indexedDB, fetch, XMLHttpRequest, or navigator.sendBeacon anywhere in the two files -- consistent with the README's stated no-network/no-storage claim and with the ui-requirements.test.ts REQ-015 assertion already covering this as a regression test.
- Six buttons drive data-command from a fixed, static HTML attribute set (penUp/penDown/forward/backward/turnLeft/turnRight); there is no free-text input, URL parameter, or postMessage channel feeding into applyCommand, so command-injection/prototype-pollution vectors are not present. (Minor robustness note, not a security defect: applyCommand's switch has no default case, so a manually-forced invalid command string, e.g. via devtools, would fall through to an implicit undefined return and could crash a subsequent render; this requires the user to already have full control of their own browser session and has no cross-user or data-exposure impact.)
- No secrets, credentials, or environment values are read or embedded in any of the new files.
- Scan-stage evidence (job 19-27, same headSha) already reports CodeQL, dependency audit, and secret scanning passed; this review treats that as present evidence, not an assumed pass, and independently corroborates it by inspecting the actual diff content described above rather than only trusting the scan summary.
